blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
High-stakes negotiation is, above all, a test of emotional self-regulation. Commercial, political and sometimes personal stakes combine to produce a pressure that lesser negotiators cannot quite think clearly through. The edge belongs to whoever can remain thoughtful when everyone else, including themselves, is being pulled by urgency.

Experienced negotiators prepare for three different worlds before a significant meeting: the best realistic outcome, the worst acceptable one, and the walk-away point beyond which no deal is better than the deal on offer. Knowing those three in advance makes it far easier to decide, in the room, whether a difficult concession moves them towards or away from acceptable. Those who negotiate without that clarity end up conceding in the direction of the other side's energy, rather than their own interests.

Language in these moments is surgical. "Were we to accept those terms, we would need a corresponding shift on payment" carries more precision than "we want a better deal". Conditional and subjunctive forms create cognitive room to trade without publicly committing. They are the quiet tools of people who close complicated deals.

items.q: According to the text, high-stakes negotiation is, above all, a test of…
options: emotional self-regulation
legal expertise
public speaking
financial modelling
items.why: "High-stakes negotiation is, above all, a test of emotional self-regulation."

items.q: What are the three 'worlds' an experienced negotiator prepares?
options: Short-term, medium-term and long-term value
Best realistic outcome, worst acceptable one, and the walk-away point
Opening bid, counter-offer and mid-point
Legal, commercial and political scenarios
items.why: "the best realistic outcome, the worst acceptable one, and the walk-away point".

items.q: Why is "Were we to accept those terms, we would need a corresponding shift on payment" described as more surgical than "we want a better deal"?
options: It is shorter and easier to say
It hides the negotiator's real intentions entirely
It is precise and trades without publicly committing
It is more aggressive
items.why: "carries more precision… create cognitive room to trade without publicly committing."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The most valuable negotiator is the one who responds fastest to pressure.
Staying calm under urgency is a competitive advantage.
A clear walk-away point strengthens a negotiator's position.
Subjunctive language can keep options open.
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza quem permanece pensativo sob urgência, não quem reage rápido à pressão.

items.q: What does "conceding in the direction of the other side's energy" suggest about unprepared negotiators?
options: They rely too heavily on written contracts
They let the other party's momentum, not their own interests, decide their concessions
They negotiate more aggressively than prepared ones
They always walk away too early
items.why: Inferência: sem clareza sobre os três mundos, cedem levados pela pressão alheia, não pelos próprios interesses.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver conduzindo a negociação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for the revised proposal. I've read it twice, and I want to be measured about how I respond, because I think we are closer than the room feels.

Let me be candid about where I sit. The volume commitment you're asking for over five years is significant, and, as things stand, I can't sign to it at this price. That's not a tactic — it genuinely sits beyond the point at which this deal works for us.

So let me put something on the table conditionally. Were we to accept the volume you've outlined, we would need the payment terms moved from thirty days to sixty, and an index clause protecting us if input costs move sharply. Give me those two, and I think we have the shape of an agreement.

Should you feel unable to move on payment, that's a legitimate position, and I'd rather know now than discover it after our lawyers have spent three weeks drafting. I'm not in a hurry. I'd genuinely rather walk away today with a clear no than sign something neither of us can live with in year three. But I don't think that's where we are. Take the afternoon, talk to your principals, and come back to me.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver say about the volume commitment at the current price?
options: He can accept it immediately
He needs the volume doubled
He wants to remove the volume clause entirely
As things stand, he cannot sign to it at that price
items.why: "the volume commitment… as things stand, I can't sign to it at this price."

items.q: What two things does Oliver ask for in exchange for accepting the volume?
options: Payment moved to fifteen days and a penalty clause
A lower price and a shorter contract
Payment moved to sixty days and an index clause on input costs
A larger deposit and exclusivity
items.why: "payment terms moved from thirty days to sixty, and an index clause protecting us if input costs move sharply."

items.q: Why does Oliver say he'd rather know now if they can't move on payment?
options: To pressure them into signing faster
To avoid wasting three weeks of legal drafting on an unworkable deal
Because his lawyers are unavailable later
Because he has another buyer waiting
items.why: "I'd rather know now than discover it after our lawyers have spent three weeks drafting."

items.q: What does Oliver's statement "I'm not in a hurry" most likely signal?
options: That he expects the deal to take years to close
That the meeting is running late
That he has no interest in the deal
That he holds a strong walk-away position and won't be rushed into a bad deal
items.why: Inferência: sinaliza paciência estratégica e um ponto de retirada claro — o calmo tem mais alavancagem.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's overall approach?
options: Calm and conditional, trading precisely while keeping options open
Aggressive and threatening
Vague and non-committal
Eager to close at any cost
items.why: Inferência: usa linguagem condicional ("Were we to…", "Should you…") para negociar com precisão sem se comprometer publicamente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Below our walk-away point, no deal is better than the deal on offer." A walk-away point is…
options: the opening bid you present first
the moment the other side leaves the room
the limit beyond which you would rather have no deal
the mid-point between two offers
items.why: Walk-away point = ponto de retirada: o limite além do qual nenhum acordo é preferível.

items.q: "Our BATNA was strong, so we could afford to hold firm." BATNA refers to…
options: a binding arbitration clause
your best alternative to a negotiated agreement
the average of both parties' offers
the buyer's total annual turnover
items.why: BATNA = melhor alternativa ao acordo; quanto mais forte, mais margem para não ceder.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "By moving payment to sixty days, we made a ___ concession rather than simply giving ground."
options: final
conditional
unilateral
verbal
items.why: Conditional concession = concessão condicional: cede-se algo em troca de outra coisa, não de graça.

items.q: "Any agreement had to fall inside the zone of possible agreement." This zone is…
options: the time allotted for the meeting
the range where both parties' acceptable terms overlap
the legal jurisdiction of the contract
the negotiator's personal comfort level
items.why: Zone of possible agreement (ZOPA) = zona de acordo possível: onde os limites das duas partes se sobrepõem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She opened high on purpose, using the first number as an ___ that shaped the rest of the talks."
options: index
anchor
escrow
override
items.why: Anchor = âncora: o primeiro número posto na mesa que enviesa as ofertas seguintes.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações de alto risco. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We were ready to walk away if the price didn't move." To walk away means to…
options: leave the deal on the table without agreeing
sign under protest
accept the terms reluctantly
delegate the talks to a colleague
items.why: Walk away = sair sem fechar; a disposição de não fechar é a alavancagem silenciosa.

items.q: "Let's not show our hand before they've made their offer." To show your hand means to…
options: raise your opening price
shake on the agreement
reveal your true position or intentions
put the terms in writing
items.why: Show your hand = revelar sua real posição — a linguagem condicional serve justamente para não fazer isso.

items.q: "The buyer tried to lowball us with an opening figure far below market." To lowball means to…
options: make a deliberately very low offer
add hidden fees later
propose a fair mid-point
accept the first number offered
items.why: Lowball = oferecer deliberadamente muito abaixo, para ancorar a negociação para baixo.

items.q: "Before we commit, let's hold out for the index clause." To hold out for something means to…
options: refuse to settle until you get it
quietly drop the demand
postpone the whole discussion
concede it to the other side
items.why: Hold out for = insistir e não fechar até obter aquilo que se quer.

items.q: "We finally hammered out the payment terms after two long sessions." To hammer out means to…
options: sign without reading the detail
escalate the dispute to lawyers
reach an agreement through hard, detailed effort
abandon the negotiation
items.why: Hammer out = negociar com esforço até chegar a um acordo sobre os detalhes.
